---
title: "Proof of concept: four live languages, figures included"
---

```{r}
#| include: false
library(tidyverse)
source("_common.R")
source("setup/load_data.R")
source("_engines.R")
```

The same histogram, drawn four times by four different programs.

## R

```{r}
#| label: poc-r
d <- book_data("ch01-heights")
ggplot(d, aes(x = height)) +
  geom_histogram(aes(y = after_stat(density)), bins = 30,
                 fill = "steelblue", colour = "white") +
  stat_function(fun = dnorm, args = list(mean = 68, sd = 4),
                colour = "firebrick", linewidth = 1) +
  labs(x = "height (inches)", y = "density") +
  theme_book()
```

## SPSS (via PSPP)

```{pspp}
#| label: poc-spss
INSERT FILE='data/sim/ch01-heights.sps'.
GRAPH /HISTOGRAM = height.
```

## Julia

```{julia}
#| label: poc-julia
using CSV, DataFrames, Plots, Distributions
d = CSV.read("data/sim/ch01-heights.csv", DataFrame)

histogram(d.height, bins = 30, normalize = :pdf, legend = false,
          xlabel = "height (inches)", ylabel = "density")
plot!(x -> pdf(Normal(68, 4), x), 54, 82, linewidth = 2, color = :firebrick)
```

## Python

```{python}
#| label: poc-python
import pandas as pd, numpy as np
import matplotlib.pyplot as plt
from scipy.stats import norm

d = pd.read_csv("data/sim/ch01-heights.csv")

plt.hist(d.height, bins=30, density=True, color="steelblue", edgecolor="white")
grid = np.linspace(54, 82, 400)
plt.plot(grid, norm.pdf(grid, 68, 4), color="firebrick", linewidth=2)
plt.xlabel("height (inches)"); plt.ylabel("density")
plt.show()
```
